title: The source metadata table says Version 1 while the file family is v2
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx
description: The document control table of the source states Version 1 and Date 28 October 2026, while the file itself is named 'Document Management Design v2' and no v3 exists in the folder. A next version can only be numbered from the family that the folder holds, so the next version is 3 and the Version 1 statement of the source cannot be carried forward as the version row without contradicting the file name.
evidence: Source metadata table rows 'Version | 1' and 'Date | 28 October 2026'; file name 'Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx'; no other file of the family in 05 Technical architecture.
proposed: Number the realigned document 3, keep '1, 28 October 2026' visible in the Source version row and the change log, and align the metadata Version row with the file name at the next review.

title: The case match of an intake item has no consumed contract in Architecture v5
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Section 2 says the intake agent matches the document to the case by case number, account or name, and section 6 scopes a read to the case, so rwb-document needs the case identity and the case scope of the caller. Architecture v5 slide 16 lists no rwb-case REST operation among the IN contracts of rwb-document, and the Ownership Map has no consumed-operation row for P5 against P3. The design therefore needs a stated reading of how the case is reached.
evidence: Source section 2 bullet 4 and section 6 bullet 2; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 IN line ('POST /documents, GET /documents/{id}, /cases/{id}/documents, POST /documents/generate; AgentRunCompleted; DocumentIntakeWorkflow'); Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet: no P3 operation with consumer P5.
proposed: Read the case identity and the case scope through the case contract of P3 rwb-case over REST (one hop, 2 s timeout) with a contract fake, class C, and record it as a consumed contract of P5.

title: The legal hold is a case operation in the Ownership Map and a hub rule in the source design
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: The source makes a legal hold on a case or document stop expiry, and places the retention class and the hold together in the document hub. The Ownership Map gives POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold to P3 rwb-case and gives rwb_document no legal-hold table, while Architecture v5 slide 16 lists retention under P5. The document therefore has to say where the hold is recorded and how rwb-document learns of it.
evidence: Source section 7 bullet 2; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet row 'POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold' with owner P3; Tables sheet rows for P5: no legal_hold table; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 OUT line ('metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures, retention').
proposed: Record the hold in rwb-case (P3), have rwb-document read it before an expiry is proposed, and keep retention_rule and retention_action in rwb_document.

title: e-Discovery is described with no operation in the Ownership Map
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: Section 7 requires e-Discovery to return every document for a named population with metadata and versions. The 17 P5 rows of the Endpoints sheet hold no e-discovery operation and no population resource, so the interface that serves the requirement is not specified by any source.
evidence: Source section 7 bullet 4; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet: 17 operations with owner P5, none for e-discovery or a population.
proposed: Serve e-Discovery with GET /documents of rwb-document and the case, type and date filters, returning metadata and the version list; add a dedicated operation only if the legal team needs one.

title: Document types and checklists are reference data in the source and P5 tables in the Ownership Map
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: Section 3 adds further types 'as reference data', and the R-PREC default ruling of Rules v1 R3 gives parameters and reference data to P3 rwb-case with the DP-07 reference-data contract. The Ownership Map gives document_type, document_checklist_item and case_document_check to P5 rwb-document. The two readings differ on who owns the type list and through whose contract another service reads it.
evidence: Source section 3 closing paragraph; Rules v1 R3 default rulings ('Parameters and reference data (E1-042, E1-043): P3 rwb-case', 'Reference data, LOV: rwb-case') and DP-07; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet rows document_type, document_checklist_item, case_document_check with owner P5.
proposed: Keep the document type list and the checklist in rwb_document (P5) and let other services read them through the P5 contract; do not copy them into the rwb-case reference data.

title: The intake job has no mechanism or frequency in the source design
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Section 2 says the scanner folder is 'picked up by the intake job' and gives no frequency, no owner and no mechanism. Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-12 as every 15 minutes, owner rwb-document, mechanism 'event plus KEDA workers', and slide 16 puts OCR, classify and extract in DocumentIntakeWorkflow. The source alone cannot be built from.
evidence: Source section 2 row 'Branch scanner' and row 'Mailroom'; Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-12 row; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 TMP line.
proposed: Run JOB-12 as a 15-minute Temporal trigger that starts DocumentIntakeWorkflow, with KEDA workers scaling on the intake queue.

title: The search index and the masking rows sit with different owners
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: Section 6 says masked fields are not searchable, so the rule has to be applied where the index is built (rwb_document, P5) and where the response is shaped. The masking rows are masking_rule in rwb_access (P4) and the source neither names the table nor says whether the index holds the clear value. No source states which service filters the index.
evidence: Source section 6 bullets 1 and 4; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet row masking_rule with owner P4 and rows document, document_field with owner P5.
proposed: Index no personal field in clear form, mask every response at the P5 API against the masking_rule rows of rwb-access, and test the index with a national ID search.

title: E-signature is named in the type table and nowhere else
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: The settlement agreement arrives 'generated; e-signature or scan', and Architecture v5 slide 41 lists signatures under P5, with signature_request a P5 table in the Ownership Map. No source gives the request interface, the party model or the result event, and the callers that need a signature (S2 rwb-treatment for a settlement, S6 rwb-debtsale for a lot pack) are not stated in this document.
evidence: Source section 3 row 'Settlement agreement'; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 OUT line ('signatures'); Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet row signature_request with owner P5.
proposed: Record the request in signature_request (P5) and expose it as an activity contract on queue rwb-document, called by the owning service that needs the signature.

title: The storage is 'Blob storage' in the source and Azure Blob with a WORM container in Architecture v5
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Sections 1 and 2 name 'Blob storage' and a write-once container, with DL27 still open on storage, backup and legal hold. Architecture v5 slide 16 names Azure Blob (WORM) as the file store of P5 and gives the volume (files, 2.8 TB by 2031). The source wording is older and does not name the platform.
evidence: Source section 1 row 'Storage' and section 2 bullet 2; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 FILE line ('Azure Blob (WORM): files, 2.8 TB by 2031').
proposed: Name the store as Azure Blob (WORM) with the claim-check pattern and the 2.8 TB by 2031 planning figure, and keep DL27 open for the backup and legal-hold detail.

title: The overdue-original task has no owner queue
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: Section 5 records an overdue original as 'Task to document services; MSG-P5-004 on the case'. Tasks, queues and allocation belong to P3 rwb-case in the Ownership Map, and rwb_document has no task table, so the source sentence does not say which service raises the task or where the officer sees it.
evidence: Source section 5 row 'Overdue'; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: task and queue resources with owner P3, none with owner P5.
proposed: Raise the task through the task contract of rwb-case (P3), carry MSG-P5-004 on the case, and keep the custody row in rwb_document.
